Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

UltraFeedback: Boosting Language Models with Scaled AI Feedback (2310.01377v2) · paper method: The impact statement warns that AI feedback can favor answer position, response length or style, leading to inaccurate or unfair annotations and evaluations; the reported feedback pipeline does not eliminate these risks by construction.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

UltraFeedback: Boosting Language Models with Scaled AI Feedback (2310.01377v2) · paper method: On 400 sampled response comparisons, 100 each from UltraFeedback, AlpacaEval, Evol-Instruct and UltraChat, three independent student judges gave win/tie/lose labels; GPT-4’s mean agreement with individual judges was 59.7% and agreement with their majority was 68.6%, including ties.

cohort9.claim.ultrafeedback.human-agreement

  • Judge agreement measures consistency, not verified factual correctness; the later 266-pair evaluation uses a distinct filtered denominator.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

UltraFeedback: Boosting Language Models with Scaled AI Feedback (2310.01377v2) · paper method: For each of 63,967 instructions, UltraFeedback samples four different models from a 17-model pool, producing 255,864 completions; model family/size diversity and varying system principles are intended to reduce style–quality confounding.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

UltraFeedback: Boosting Language Models with Scaled AI Feedback (2310.01377v2) · paper method: GPT-4 scores each prompt’s four completions together using documented 1–5 rubrics for instruction-following, truthfulness, honesty and helpfulness, with score rationales; a separate tutor-style prompt produces an overall critique per completion.
